![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14252915/assets/d69e6b6550f7e4cae0785daaa19c0a52382a595c40309dccd1d832dbc6d2f82f.png)

Which of the following represents the shaded region above as a type I region in two-dimensional space?
question.worked_solution:
A type I region can be written as

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,a\le x\le b,\,g(x)\le y\le f(x)\},
$$

where $f$ and $g$ are continuous functions.

To express the given region as a type I region, we first rewrite all of the given curves as functions of $x:$

$$
x=\sqrt{y-1}+1\,⟹\,y=(x-1)^{2}+1
$$

The function $y=-(x-1)^{2}+3$ is already written as a function of $x.$

Notice that the region lies between the vertical lines $x=1$ and $x=2.$ So, we have $1\le x\le 2.$

We draw a vertical arrow through the region to determine the lower function $g(x)$ and the upper function $f(x).$ A vertical line should intersect the region in a single interval only for it to be a type I region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14252915/assets/942a39f885e6f88bef997e27914d05359be86ae1d6204f3834f0829ce4b81136.png)

The vertical line enters the region through the lower function $y=(x-1)^{2}+1$ and leaves through the upper function $y=-(x-1)^{2}+3.$ So, we have $(x-1)^{2}+1\le y\le -(x-1)^{2}+3.$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,1\le x\le 2,\,(x-1)^{2}+1\le y\le -(x-1)^{2}+3\}.
$$
